excerpts: ## The next chapter of Copilot is here The Ignite keynote is under way, and Satya is talking about how the way we work with AI has evolved, and why it was key for Microsoft Copilot to do the same. Collaboration is at the core of [the new Copilot](https://aka.ms/MicrosoftIgnite26Blog) , creating a connected system where people and AI work together with the context, choice and control organizations need to get more done. **Home** , where **Chat** and **Cowork** come together, and **Office in Copilot** , which fully integrate **Word** , **Excel** and **PowerPoint** into Copilot, are now both generally available. Features like **Code** , where people can turn plain language into working apps, and **Autopilot** , a persistent, proactive agent designed to help you be more productive, are now rolling out to Frontier customers. **Copilot Managed Runtime,** which securely hosts what you build, is now generally available. **Today,** currently rolling out to private preview in Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot app, helps people stay on top of their work by surfacing key priorities and preparing next steps. The experience includes the **Today Brief,** which provides a personalized morning briefing and the **Today Feed, which** builds on the morning briefing by automatically refreshing throughout the day as new emails, messages and meetings come in. Additionally, Satya is announcing **Copilot Workspaces** , which brings teams, their work and Copilot together in a shared space in the Microsoft Copilot app. And coming soon, teams will be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces, so humans and agents can collaborate in one space and team members can shift from doing the work to directing it.

## Microsoft, Salesforce announce Salesforce in Copilot, Teams and Fabric Satya is now announcing Copilotforce, new integrations of Salesforce across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Fabric. This brings Salesforce customer context, business processes and actions into the Microsoft tools people use every day. [**Salesforce in Copilot**](https://aka.ms/AA1457n5) is a new plugin now available in preview. It features more than 38 prebuilt sales skills and connects customer context with the work happening across the business. From within Copilot, sellers can securely retrieve customer information and take supported business actions within their existing Salesforce permissions through authenticated Salesforce MCP access. Sellers can then put that context to work across Microsoft 365 with Work IQ, the intelligence layer powering Copilot.

## Microsoft IQ makes the most of organizational expertise In today’s fast-paced business climate, many companies have access to frontier models. But gaining true value from AI occurs when it benefits from the unique knowledge inside your organization, curated by the people who know your business best and shared across the entire company. Satya is now talking about [**Microsoft IQ**](https://aka.ms/miq-ignitelaunchblog) , a new enterprise context management platform that allows users to build plugins that capture their know-how, context, skills and tools, creating their unique IQ and compounding their intelligence over time. It brings together Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ, in addition to over 350 third-party connectors to create an organization’s enterprise context. This gives AI a governed understanding of the organization, so you don’t have to explain how your business works every time you build an agent. As the way we work with AI has evolved, so has Microsoft Copilot. The new Copilot includes **Home** , the single starting point for Chat and Cowork; **Auto** , the smart router for Copilot that dynamically picks the right models and effort for your task, optimizing for quality, speed and cost; and **Word** , **Excel** and **PowerPoint** in Copilot to create and collaborate on files alongside your conversation. They will be able to: Understand spend: Insight into what’s driving cost across agents, services, models and users. Drive business value: Measure the value of AI assistance for specific jobs and tasks through measures such as success rate, user satisfaction and assisted hours. Optimize ROI: Forecast cost scenarios, act on recommendations and ask questions in plain language, then work with IT to adjust guardrails for chargebacks. Autopilot is rolling out to Frontier customers **Autopilot** is Microsoft’s first enterprise-grade, long-running agent for personal productivity. It will live in an organization’s tenant with its own identity, memory and access to tools, and can follow up on threads, run recurring work and continue a project without waiting for another prompt. Designed for collaboration, colleagues will be able to @mention a person’s Autopilot in a Teams channel or group chat to ask for information or request supported actions. Autopilot is designed for security: Actions it takes (even on a user’s behalf) aretied to its own agent ID and safety-checked, and it is visible and manageable by admins. Copilot Managed Runtime is now generally available, with new capabilities Copilot Managed Runtime provides Microsoft-managed hosting and execution for applications, separate from where those applications are created. Builders can start with experiences, including Copilot Code, Copilot Cowork and Microsoft Copilot Studio, or use compatible third-party development tools. When an app is published to Copilot Managed Runtime, organizations gain a common way to host, run and govern it. With the **general availability of Copilot Managed Runtime** , Microsoft is expanding this product, giving apps built across Microsoft Copilot and compatible third-party development tools an optional data backend with services from Microsoft Fabric. With the new integration, applications that optionally need persistent data or additional backend capabilities can use Fabric as their underlying data foundation out of the box. Fabric can provide backend capabilities including database, storage and data APIs, while Copilot Managed Runtime continues to provide the application hosting and enterprise management layer. The integration brings together flexible app creation, Microsoft-managed hosting and governance and an **optional Fabric data backend** , allowing organizations to choose the development experience that fits their needs while providing a consistent path for running applications in their Microsoft environment. Microsoft is also announcing **Agents and Workflows in Copilot Managed Runtime** . The first iteration will allow users to build custom Copilot Studio agents and workflows locally, make modifications with their dev tool of choice and then publish to Copilot Studio using the CLI. This also gives developers a collaborative approach to agent development on Copilot Studio, alongside version control through platforms like GitHub. Once in a workspace, team members can work together on shared documents while Copilot connects the dots across the work, surfacing what changed, what remains unresolved and which actions need attention so everyone can quickly catch up and keep the work moving. And coming soon, teams will be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces, so humans and agents can collaborate in one space and team members can shift from doing the work to directing it. Copilot Workspaces is available in the Copilot app through the Frontier program. [**Learn more about this news**](https://aka.ms/MicrosoftIgnite26Blog) .

Easily build secure apps with Copilot Code **Copilot Code** will empower everyone to build dashboards, trackers and apps with natural language, using the same agentic technology as GitHub Copilot. Home in the Microsoft Copilot app **Home** , [announced in September](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/09/25/introducing-the-new-copilot-with-home-code-and-autopilot/) and now rolling out worldwide, is the new starting point in Copilot, bringing Chat and Cowork together so people can easily move between asking quick questions and delegating complex workflows. Updates include two new capabilities when using **Auto** , Copilot’s smart router, which dynamically picks the right model and effort for your task: Auto now recommends moving from Chat to Cowork for complex tasks to help users select the mode that offers the best response. Auto in Cowork will use Microsoft-Decision-1.1, a fast, cost-effective decision model, to dynamically pick effort levels according to a user’s task. Bringing models, data and familiar tools together reduces integration work for developers building AI-powered applications. **Built-in AI model management** , in preview, will manage generative and ranking models alongside data, while **AI Functions** and **AI Pipelines** , in preview, will enable developers to invoke models directly from SQL queries without impacting application performance.

Microsoft Fabric HorizonDB brings PostgreSQL to Fabric in preview **Microsoft Fabric HorizonDB** , a new database offering in preview, will bring PostgreSQL, one of developers’ most popular databases, directly into Microsoft Fabric. It will connect applications, data analysis and AI in one place.

Fabric HorizonDB is serverless PostgreSQL built for these patterns. Databases will provision in seconds and scale automatically with demand. Idle databases will pause, then resume when the next query arrives.

Fabric HorizonDB will also be enabled for Fabric apps. It will provide a managed backend with data APIs, authentication, storage and hosting, so developers can go from idea to a running app with PostgreSQL built in.

Query across operational and analytical data Fabric HorizonDB will bring live operational data and analytics in OneLake together, so applications can act on both. **Translytical queries** A single PostgreSQL query will combine live data in Fabric HorizonDB with analytical data in OneLake, running on Fabric Data Warehouse’s scale-out compute.
**Mirroring** Fabric HorizonDB tables will copy into Fabric for analytics, with no separate pipelines.
**Reverse ETL** Enriched data from Fabric Data Warehouse will flow back into Fabric HorizonDB, where apps and agents can read it quickly. **[Learn more about this news.](https://aka.ms/AAncdv4)**

**Simpler migration and modernization.** Azure Database Migration Service (DMS) support for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL data migration is now in preview. Combined with assessment, schema conversion and application conversion in the Microsoft PostgreSQL extension for VS Code, it will provide a first-party path from preparation and code conversion to data movement.

Additionally, customers will be able to use Azure DMS, in preview, to move existing Azure Database for PostgreSQL workloads to Azure HorizonDB through a seamless, managed experience. DMS will handle connectivity validation, data copy, continuous synchronization for online migrations, monitoring and planned cutover, simplifying modernization on a high-performance, scalable PostgreSQL platform.

**More choice for performance and scale.** Burstable v2 compute, in preview, will add flexibility for development and workloads with changing demands. Cobalt 200, now generally available for Azure Database for PostgreSQL, adds Microsoft-designed Arm64-based compute alongside Intel and AMD x64-based options. Customers can choose the architecture that best fits their workloads as they modernize and scale on Azure.

**Stronger protection for sensitive workloads.** AMD v6 confidential compute, now generally available, helps protect data in use. Point-in-time restore immutability, also generally available, helps protect backups against changes or deletion.

**Expanded backup and resilience.** Azure Backup for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server and elastic clusters version 2, in preview, will support larger databases with snapshot-based backups and direct restore. Same-zone to zone-redundant high availability conversion, now generally available, helps protect against availability zone failures without recreating servers.

**Expanded backup and resilience.** Azure Backup for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server and elastic clusters version 2, in preview, will support larger databases with snapshot-based backups and direct restore. Same-zone to zone-redundant high availability conversion, now generally available, helps protect against availability zone failures without recreating servers. These enhancements strengthen PostgreSQL on Azure for critical and regulated applications. Organizations can expand their use of PostgreSQL as their needs grow while maintaining performance, protection and resilience. [**Learn more about this news**](https://aka.ms/Ignite26/Postgres_on_Azure) .

Dynamic Agent Risk within Agent 365 in preview **Dynamic Agent Risk** , in preview, will leverage Microsoft’s security context engine to fuse runtime signals (identity, access, data, endpoints, cloud and network), posture and blast radius into a comprehensive agent risk assessment — removing the need for security teams to stitch together siloed security tools to gain a complete agent risk understanding. Dynamic Agent Risk will follow the agent as it takes new actions, becomes the target of malicious activity or receives code or model updates — always updating as risk changes — and serve as a core primitive, along with Agent Registry, that is visible across Microsoft 365 Admin Center and Defender, Entra, Intune and Purview. Additionally, a partnership with risk management platforms Check Point, Cyera, Darktrace and Zenity brings partner agent-security signals into Microsoft Sentinel and uses them as evidence in Microsoft-calculated agent risk for Agent 365. The planned flow uses dedicated agent-risk connectors and an agreed data schema. Sentinel analytics rules turn incoming partner signals into alerts. Microsoft Security then correlates supported alerts to agents and incorporates them into its risk assessment. Microsoft computes the unified low, medium or high level of risk, while contributing providers remain visible as data sources. The overall risk design considers runtime risk, exposure and blast radius, with partner signals contributing runtime evidence. This authoritative understanding of agent risk will form the foundation for comprehensive runtime risk mitigation and containment at speed and scale, working 24/7 via Microsoft Perception.

Codename MDASH, a new agentic code security system, available in preview **Codename MDASH, Microsoft’s agentic code security system** , is in preview for eligible organizations. It adds new capabilities that will help security and engineering teams work from validated findings. Advances in AI models are changing how vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited. Codename MDASH uses more than 100 specialized AI agents in a four-stage pipeline. It will map the attack surface, scan code, validate findings through agent debate, remove duplicates and, where possible, reproduce findings with a triggering input. New capabilities for Codename MDASH include: **Quality improvements:** Reduces low-quality results and false positives, so teams can spend less time triaging and more time on actionable vulnerabilities. **Repository sharding:** Analyzes large repositories by partitioning codebases into logical units, using fewer tokens per scan. **Progress visibility:** Makes scan stages, completed work, elapsed time and result availability more visible to better understand scan progress. **Broader MAI Cyber model support:** Codename MDASH now supports more of the MAI Cyber model family, including MAI Cyber 1.1 Flash, and will use MAI-Cyber-2 once evaluation testing is complete, improving efficiency while maintaining the quality of security findings. Introducing Windows Server 2028 For enterprises that depend on Windows-based applications and infrastructure, Windows Server provides a trusted foundation that extends existing skills, tools and investments while supporting critical workloads from the datacenter to the edge. **Windows Server 2028** is now in preview. It will strengthen the infrastructure organizations already depend on while extending Windows Server to enterprise AI inference and hybrid intelligence. Features include: **Stronger security** : Windows Server 2028 will strengthen security by default with a hardened Server Core configuration, a new security baseline, Trusted Launch for virtual machines, post-quantum cryptography and automated certificate management. These capabilities will help protect identities, workloads and encrypted communications while helping organizations prepare for emerging threats and evolving regulatory requirements. **Accelerated enterprise infrastructure:** Organizations will be able to improve the performance and efficiency of storage- and data-intensive workloads with NVMe over Fabrics, native NVMe storage and the ability to boot from the Resilient File System—helping them get more from modern infrastructure and accelerated hardware. **Simplified administration and management at scale:** Organizations will be able to manage Windows Server more consistently across datacenters, the cloud and remote locations using Microsoft Intune, Azure Arc, Windows Admin Center and vMode. **Enterprise hybrid intelligence:** Windows Server 2028 will expand the infrastructure organizations already trust to support enterprise AI inference close to business-critical applications and data. Investments include: **Software** : Supported runtimes and inference platforms, including Windows ML, Foundry Local, vLLM and Llama.cpp. **Security** : Microsoft Execution Containers and multilayer protection spanning hardware, the operating system, hypervisor and runtimes. **Governance and control** : Integration with Agent 365 to help organizations govern AI across their environments. **Hardware** : Support for accelerated AI silicon, including the AMD MI350P accelerator and the NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip. Together, these capabilities help organizations run AI on infrastructure they control while connecting to Azure as part of a hybrid AI architecture. The security, performance and management features are in preview through the Windows Server Insider Program. Hybrid intelligence features are available to a limited number of customers through an early access program. Hardware requirements apply. [**Learn more about this news**](https://aka.ms/WindowsServer2028Announcement) .

Azure Cosmos DB improves development, retrieval and data protection Azure Cosmos DB is introducing seven updates that improve search and retrieval quality, help developers design and evolve applications and strengthen protection for production data. They include: **Developer tools and application design** **Azure Cosmos DB Shell:** Now generally available in Visual Studio Code and the Azure portal, the shell gives developers interactive access to explore resources, query and manage data, and enable AI-assisted workflows through MCP integration. **AI-assisted data modeler and other updates in Azure Cosmos DB extension for VS Code:** Now in preview, these updates will bring account insights, AI-powered recommendations and guided data modeling for partition keys and container configurations directly into VS Code. **Rust SDK for Azure Cosmos DB:** Now generally available, the SDK provides a native Rust client with built-in performance and resilience capabilities to help teams build reliable distributed production applications. **Search and retrieval quality** **Semantic reranker:** Now generally available, this capability uses an AI model to evaluate candidate search results and reorder them according to the meaning and context of the query and content. **FuzzyBM25 score projection updates in full-text search:** Now generally available, these updates expand full-text search by making relevance scores available to applications. **Data movement and production protection** **Azure Backup for Azure Cosmos DB:** Now generally available, Azure Backup adds an independent, vault-based protection layer for centralized backup policies, monitoring, retention and recovery. Together, these updates support the Azure Cosmos DB application lifecycle: improving retrieval relevance, helping teams design and evolve applications and protecting production data. Azure DocumentDB expands developer tools, sovereignty and security Azure DocumentDB is introducing five feature updates to help developers build applications, apply more-granular access controls and run MongoDB-compatible workloads across hybrid environments. **Faster development and provisioning** **Azure DocumentDB extension for Visual Studio Code:** Now generally available, the extension lets developers connect to clusters, browse databases and collections, inspect documents and run queries—all within Visual Studio Code.

Azure Chaos Studio Workspaces, AKS extension now generally available Azure Chaos Studio Workspaces and the Azure Chaos Studio extension for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) are now generally available, expanding the ways organizations can test how applications respond to and recover from disruptions. These updates expand Azure Chaos Studio, a managed service that allows organizations to introduce controlled failures into applications to test how they respond and recover. Azure Chaos Studio Workspaces provide a simpler way to organize and run resilience tests. Organizations can define the resources they want to test and apply reusable scenarios that represent disruptions, such as the loss of an availability zone or database failover. This makes it easier to test how an application responds to realistic disruptions and repeat those tests over time. The Azure Chaos Studio extension for AKS brings resilience testing to applications running on AKS. The extension requires fewer permissions to run experiments, providing a more secure way for organizations to introduce controlled disruptions to Kubernetes pods and observe how applications respond and recover. These updates help organizations validate whether applications can recover from disruptions as expected. By introducing failures in a controlled environment, organizations can identify weaknesses and make improvements before similar failures occur unexpectedly. [**Learn more about this news**](https://aka.ms/chaosstudio/workspaces-ga) **.** Azure expands confidential computing for protecting highly sensitive data Microsoft Azure is expanding its confidential computing offerings to help organizations unlock more value from data, scale AI innovation and collaborate with greater confidence and control — protecting not only where data is stored and how it moves, but also how it is processed. Three offerings are now in preview: VR72 multi-GPU confidential computing that will advance Azure’s confidential computing AI roadmap and open a path to protect large models that extend beyond a single GPU. Azure Confidential Enclaves and AKS Kata CoCo confidential containers, whichwillcreate a smaller trusted execution environment within a broader virtual machine. This will help businesses narrow what must be trusted and verified instead of placing that trust in the entire surrounding system. Azure Confidential Clean Room, which will enable organizations to bring data together for multiparty analytics while helping protect each participant’s sensitive raw data from other collaborators and cloud operators. This will open new opportunities to generate shared insights without giving up control of protected information. [**Learn more about this news.**](https://aka.ms/acc-ignite2026)

Azure expands agentic operations with new monitoring, AI capabilities Agentic operations bring AI agents directly into Azure, helping teams investigate issues faster, optimize resources continuously and act with greater confidence. **Expanded** **agentic capabilities** **across Azure Monitor, Azure Copilot and Azure SRE Agent** will deliver richer operational context, stronger governance and a common foundation for operational agents, while keeping humans in control. **New natural language capabilities** , now generally available in Azure Monitor, help users plan and deploy cloud workloads. Azure Copilot spaces and custom skills, in preview, will allow teams to tailor agents for faster, more efficient and accurate operations while carrying persistent context. Users will also be able to extend agentic operations to Oracle and SAP through Azure Workload Center, in preview, for workload health monitoring and configuration validation. New Azure SRE Agent capabilities, in preview, will enable **secure agentic operations at enterprise scale** . Customer-managed keys will give teams full control of agent data, while Entra Agent ID and Agent 365 integration will provide users with a consistent way to discover, govern, audit and manage agents throughout their lifecycle. Cross-agent communications will enable context and task-sharing across agents for faster incident resolution. Azure SRE Agent will also integrate with Microsoft Teams and extend investigations across multicloud environments. These updates will help organizations move from agent experimentation to deployment across complex production environments. Azure Monitor health models, now generally available, **turn telemetry into actionable health context** . Users can translate telemetry into a real-time health graph that connects application architecture, dependencies and business priorities. This helps teams understand what is affected, distinguish platform issues from application failures and prioritize incidents by business impact. The same context enables AI agents to investigate issues, identify root causes, recommend remediation and automate workflows. [**Learn more about this news**](https://aka.ms/ignite2026/agenticops) . Azure infrastructure foundation for production AI applications and agents New capabilities built for the unique needs of production AI applications—from agent networking and security to isolation, confidentiality, context and state—will span an AI foundation across compute, storage and networking. **A continuous experience from Microsoft Foundry to Azure:** Microsoft Foundry lets customers deploy in a fully managed environment and easily extend to Kubernetes for greater control over infrastructure performance, security and economics. Customers will now be able to deploy open-weight models and agents from Foundry to their own Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters using infrastructure, security policies and governance they already have. Teams will be able to choose GPUs and regions based on cost, latency and data residency. Foundry will handle setup, enabling the same developer workflow from experimentation through production. This will combine Foundry’s simplicity with Kubernetes’ flexibility and control. **Azure AI infrastructure** : For production AI, infrastructure directly determines agent performance, security and operating cost. Azure’s latest capabilities will optimize the underlying infrastructure for inferencing and agents, linking infrastructure decisions and business outcomes: **Agent Grid** will secure interactions among agents, models, tools and Azure services with centralized policy enforcement. **Agent Sandbox extension for AKS** will run agent-written code in sandboxes isolated at the virtual-machine level. **Flex nodes for AKS** will extend the same AKS clusters to customer servers outside Azure. **Azure Cobalt 200** virtual machines add CPU performance for services around AI models. **Openness and choice** : Azure’s AI foundation is built to stay open. Open-source projects, including vLLM, Ray and Kubernetes, keep workloads portable, and Microsoft is the largest public cloud contributor to Cloud Native Computing Foundation projects over the past three years. All capabilities are in preview except Azure Cobalt 200, which is generally available.
